node.label: Colin G Calloway
node.date_label: One Vast Winter Count (2003) · The Scratch of a Pen (2006) · The Indian World of George Washington (2018)
node.description: A historian who centres Native peoples within the history of North America. His Washington interview explains land acquisition, warfare and sovereignty as integral to the founding of the United States, while distinguishing his contextual history from a conventional great-man biography.

incident_edges.relationship: Centres Native peoples and sovereignty within the history of the early United States.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own interview explicitly argues Native history is integral to American history; this is not a claim of Indigenous identity or authority.

incident_edges.relationship: Uses Washington’s dealings with Native peoples to reconstruct a contingent era of nation-building and dispossession.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own interview distinguishes the project from biography in the usual sense and contrasts promises of sovereignty with policies eroding it.

incident_edges.relationship: Bailyn credits Calloway’s account of Indigenous devastation but disputes its broad framing of the Revolution against earlier British imperial violence and Enlightenment aspirations.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own 1995 review: opening assessment, village-study qualifications and final contextual argument. Praise and disagreement coexist. Bailyn’s contextual defense and judgments about Britain, the Revolution and Enlightenment ideals remain his claims; they are not editorial findings that dispose of Calloway’s argument. Calloway’s whole book and any reply were not read.
